idiom_name: HashMap<Long, MutableList<Entity>> with getOrPut per cell
implementation_notes: Nothing in the Kotlin standard library indexes space, so the manual realization is a HashMap<Long, MutableList<Entity>> keyed by a packed cell coordinate with getOrPut as the insert idiom, or a List<MutableList<Entity>> grid for bounded worlds. On the JVM the actual is java.util.HashMap, which is not thread-safe, so a grid shared with coroutines or renderer threads needs confinement or a concurrent map. Kotlin's collection API makes the hand grid short enough to keep as the default for runtime entity partitions; JTS or similar JVM spatial libraries fit only geometry-heavy, static workloads.
pitfalls: HashMap is not thread-safe; a partition shared between a simulation coroutine and a rendering thread needs confinement or a concurrent structure.
Tuple keys allocate on every lookup; packing the cell into a Long avoids per-query garbage on hot paths.
flatMap chains allocate intermediate lists; on large radii prefer an explicit loop writing into a reusable buffer.
